subject.title: [Feature]: Pluggable STT backend for macOS Push-to-Talk

question: Should native macOS Push-to-Talk gain a batch STT backend seam now, and should its first backend route through `tools.media.audio` or a new native/Gateway contract?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but choosing backend ownership, endpoint/auth handling, private-network policy, fallback behavior, and partial-vs-final transcript UX is a maintainer product and security decision.

options.title: Design PTT backend seam first
options.body: Add a maintainer-scoped batch-only PTT STT abstraction that keeps Apple Speech default and reuses Gateway media-audio/provider security contracts where approved.

options.title: Fold into broader ASR design
options.body: Keep this issue open as a narrow slice but resolve implementation only through the broader native custom ASR design tracked at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/46661.

options.title: Defer native backend switching
options.body: Keep native PTT on Apple Speech until maintainers decide plugin/provider surfaces are enough or a missing extension API is identified.

recommendation.title: Design PTT backend seam first
recommendation.body: Add a maintainer-scoped batch-only PTT STT abstraction that keeps Apple Speech default and reuses Gateway media-audio/provider security contracts where approved.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger has the strongest native macOS voice history and is the best available owner for the product/API boundary decision.
